metadata.title: GAM-001: CRISPR-Cas9 sgRNA Design & Cloning - Addgene Source Workflow
metadata.purpose: CRISPR-Cas9 sgRNA design and cloning using Addgene CRISPR experiment planning and gRNA design/cloning guidance. Single-guide design, oligo ordering, vector-specific annealing/ligation or Golden Gate-style cloning, and clone validation.
metadata.scope: Training/library SOP draft. Confirm against the current manufacturer/source protocol, safety documentation, institutional biosafety approval, and local lab policy before bench use.
beforeYouBegin: Define the editing goal: knockout, HDR, base editing, prime editing, CRISPRi, or CRISPRa. This SOP focuses on Cas9 knockout-style sgRNA vector cloning.
Confirm the PAM and guide length for the selected Cas enzyme and vector. Do not reuse overhangs from another vector without checking the plasmid map.
Sequence or verify the genomic region in the working cell line if polymorphisms may affect guide binding.
Design at least two to four independent guides per target for biological confidence.

steps.action: Select the target region based on biological goal. For knockout, prioritize constitutive early coding exons or essential protein domains.
Use gRNA design software to identify candidate guides with high predicted on-target activity and acceptable off-target profile.

parameters.rawText: Design at least two to four independent guides per target for biological confidence.

steps.action: Exclude guides overlapping common variants, repeats, splice ambiguity, or unintended homologous sequences when possible.
Choose final guides and record genomic coordinate, strand, PAM, exon number, predicted score, and top off-target sites.
Design forward and reverse oligos with the exact vector-required overhangs and any required leading base for U6 or other promoter expression.
steps.criticalNotes: Do not reuse overhangs from another vector without checking the plasmid map.

steps.action: Order oligos and resuspend in nuclease-free water or TE according to lab convention.
Anneal oligos using the vector protocol-compatible buffer and thermal program.
Prepare the gRNA vector using the restriction enzyme or Golden Gate-style digestion/ligation workflow specified for that plasmid.
Combine annealed oligo duplex with prepared vector and ligation/assembly reagents according to the vector-specific protocol.
Transform into competent E. coli, plate on correct antibiotic, and incubate under conditions appropriate for the plasmid backbone.
Pick colonies, miniprep plasmid DNA, and verify guide insert by Sanger sequencing using the vector primer.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Sanger sequencing must confirm correct guide sequence, orientation, and no mutation in guide scaffold/flanking region.

steps.action: Archive validated plasmid sequence, map, bacterial glycerol stock, and guide-design record.
steps.expectedResult: Validated construct and its documentation are archived.

safety: Wear lab coat, gloves, and eye protection. Follow local biosafety, chemical safety, and waste rules for live cells, yeast, chromatin, formaldehyde, nucleases, enzymes, probes, and sequencing reagents.
For genome editing or viral-vector workflows, confirm institutional approval, organism/cell-line restrictions, containment level, and waste decontamination before starting.
Use nuclease-free and contamination-controlled workflows for guide RNA, ChIP DNA, IVT/IVTT templates, and NGS libraries.
Physically separate pre-PCR and post-PCR/library-amplification areas when possible to reduce carryover contamination.
Record sample identity, construct/library ID, reagent lot, incubation program, controls, QC results, and final validation status.
